items.title: Janis Siegel interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, May 22, 2015
items.q: Jimmy Guiffre was one who taught me, when I was arranging “Four Brothers” I was going through some of the voices with him

ctx.x: Well how did you learn to do that?

Okay. I’m amazed that you picked that tune and not like “Blues for Pablo” or “Four Brothers” or any of the other things I arranged. But I learned to do it with my ears, honestly. And I would have to give credit to listening to jazz a lot, instrumentalists mainly, and hearing those kinds of voicings, and learning to understand them and learning to ask questions when needed, and I did have help and mentors along the way. Jimmy Guiffre was one who taught me, when I was arranging “Four Brothers” I was going through…
